key_points.point: Asset markets respond to the rate of change rather than absolute growth levels, so decelerating growth can cause severe market pullbacks even when corporate earnings remain near record highs.
The market entered an aggressive risk-off regime in late September, triggering widespread declines across equities, high-beta sectors, and crypto assets.
Investors must maintain humility and prepare for a broad range of economic and policy outcomes instead of assuming recent bull market returns will persist smoothly.
The market has not fully priced in a politically induced slowdown in data center construction, making current consensus valuations for AI stocks difficult to justify.
State and local ballot measures overwhelmingly favor restricting data center development, creating significant structural revenue headwinds for technology leaders.
Wall Street's failure to properly manage risk around data center bottlenecks has left tech stocks exposed to substantial downside risk.

Andy Constan of Damped Spring explains why heavier borrowing, weaker buyback support and persistent high interest rates could be changing the outlook for stocks.

On the November First Principles, Andy joins Justin Carbonneau and Jack Forehand to connect the financing of the AI boom with the earnings growth investors expect from it. Companies are spending more on their businesses, issuing securities and leaving less cash for share repurchases. At the same time, he questions whether even strong economic growth can deliver all the profits embedded in stock prices.

Andy walks through how government deficits contribute to corporate profits, what new bond and stock offerings reveal about investor demand, and why high borrowing costs matter more when they persist. He also explains how a prolonged stock-market decline could weaken spending through the wealth effect, turning a growth scare into an actual slowdown.

The discussion closes with how Andy distinguishes his long-term portfolio from tactical positions in stocks, bonds and gold, why inflation may complicate a quick policy rescue, and the evidence that would change his outlook. He remains optimistic about AI's capabilities; his test is whether customers can use it profitably at prices that also reward the companies supplying it.

key_points.point: The macroeconomic environment is shifting away from being highly supportive of equities as underlying pressures accumulate.
Equity markets are pricing in aggressive earnings expectations that cannot be met in aggregate based on realistic GDP growth forecasts.
Interest rates remaining persistently elevated rather than quickly dropping will continue to slow economic activity and weigh on asset prices.
Corporations are shifting from net buyers of equity via share buybacks to net issuers to fund capital expenditures and AI investments.
AI could eventually spark an unprecedented productivity boom that reduces the need for human labor, but that remains a speculative long-term scenario.
AI services may currently be heavily subsidized, making it unclear whether users will maintain usage when prices reflect true underlying costs.
The Federal Reserve and policymakers have become more hawkish due to elevated inflation persisting well above target for nearly six years.
Central banks will require an actual economic slowdown before easing monetary policy, which combined with elevated Treasury bond supply will keep interest rates higher for longer.
Recent equity market softness represents the start of a growth scare driven by high rates and realistic growth recalibrations.
A typical growth scare implies a drawdown of roughly 10% in the S&P 500 index.
A quick V-bottom rebound in equities will not impact real economic growth, but staying depressed or sideways for 3-4 months will slow the broader economy.
Investors should stay short equities until policymakers act or until it becomes clear whether the growth scare turns into a full economic slowdown.
Policymakers will not rush to rescue stock market pullbacks at higher levels while inflation is high, but would likely intervene if drawdowns reach deeper levels like S&P 6,000.
Rushing to buy the dip on the downside of a bubble regime is a common mistake that destroys investor capital.
A sustained resumption of the AI market rally requires real enterprise end-users demonstrating actual earnings or productivity profits from AI tokens.

The repricing in stocks relative to bonds has only unwound a few months of extreme growth expectations and has further downside potential.
Market corrections turn into bear markets when expanding risk premiums depress asset prices enough to force corporate spending cutbacks.
